title: I’m working on an AI-assisted browser RPG called TWOS: A Pup’s Adventure.
author: WideDonkey4787
selftext:
I’m working on an AI-assisted browser RPG called TWOS: A Pup’s Adventure.



It’s a story-heavy, turn-based RPG about a young wolf pup named Zenas. The current build has party members, needs/status systems, objective-driven progression, school/town exploration, and early combat.



I’m not posting this as “look, AI made a game.” I’m trying to figure out whether the actual player onboarding works.



The part I’d like feedback on is the first 10 minutes:



Does the opening make sense?

Do you understand where to go?

Is the battle UI readable?

Does the story/character setup give you any reason to continue?

Does anything softlock, break, or feel confusing?

Does the itch page explain the game clearly before launching?



AI is part of my development workflow, mostly for code direction, writing support, asset iteration, testing prompts, and debugging structure. I’m still making the design calls myself, and right now I’m trying to improve the early player experience rather than promote the project.



Playable build:

[https://thyguyx.itch.io/world-of-sopho-a-pups-adventure](https://thyguyx.itch.io/world-of-sopho-a-pups-adventure)



I’m especially interested in blunt, practical feedback. Even “I quit after two minutes because X” is useful.

comments.author: Useful_Use_6170
comments.body: Probably not my demographic, but theirs games for everyone, I’ve seen enough brainrot on Roblox to know theirs an audience for everyone. You just need to find testers that are into these types of games because you’re gonna get mixed reviews and feedback from people who are not into furry games.
